digest:
## 🔬 Major Technical Developments

### Semble – Code search for agents that uses 98% fewer tokens than grep
URL: https://github.com/MinishLab/semble
Semantic code search that dramatically cuts LLM operational costs

A 98% token reduction isn't incremental—it's structural. As AI agents become standard in development workflows, the economics of context windows become a chokepoint. This addresses a real bottleneck: grep floods agents with irrelevant matches, burning tokens on noise. Watch for enterprise devtools to acquire or clone this pattern.

### GenCAD
URL: https://gencad.github.io/
Generative AI enters mechanical CAD, potentially disrupting the Autodesk/Dassault duopoly

CAD software is a $13B market dominated by entrenched players with 30-year moats. Generative approaches to 3D design could compress engineering timelines dramatically. The question is whether outputs meet manufacturing tolerances—if so, this is the kind of capability that gets acquired quickly or spawns serious venture interest.

### Designing a Scientific Calculator from scratch in FPGA
URL: https://baltazarstudios.com/calculator/
Ground-up hardware design showcases the depth of FPGA talent outside major chip firms

Relevant for anyone tracking the custom silicon trend. As hyperscalers and AI labs design their own chips, the FPGA-to-ASIC pipeline matters. Projects like this demonstrate that serious hardware engineering capability is more distributed than the Nvidia/Broadcom narrative suggests.

## 💼 Business & Market Signals

### For Eclipse, the $2.5B Cerebras win is just the start of realizing its physical-world thesis
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/17/for-eclipse-the-2-5b-cerebras-win-is-just-the-start-of-realizing-its-physical-world-thesis/
Eclipse's Cerebras bet validates the "atoms not bits" thesis at scale

Lior Susan's decade-long contrarian position on physical-world tech is paying off at exactly the right moment. The $2.5B Cerebras outcome signals that AI infrastructure plays can generate venture-scale returns outside the software-only model. Expect more growth equity flowing into semiconductors, robotics, and manufacturing—areas PE has historically underweighted.

### Why trust is a big question at the Elon Musk-OpenAI trial
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/17/why-trust-is-a-big-question-at-the-elon-musk-openai-trial/
Altman's credibility is now a litigation variable, with implications for OpenAI's next funding round

The trial's focus on whether Altman can be trusted introduces headline risk into OpenAI's cap table. Institutional investors pricing the next round will factor in governance uncertainty. This is less about legal outcome than narrative—perception of leadership stability affects enterprise sales cycles and talent retention.

### Apple's Siri revamp could include auto-deleting chats
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/17/apples-siri-revamp-could-include-auto-deleting-chats/
Apple positions privacy as its AI differentiator against OpenAI and Google

Auto-deleting chats is a product feature, but it's really a regulatory hedge and brand play. As EU and state-level AI legislation tightens, Apple's privacy-first positioning creates enterprise sales advantages in regulated industries. The gap between Apple's on-device approach and cloud-dependent competitors becomes a procurement factor.

## 📋 Case Studies & Deep Dives

### Bun's problem may be developing in the open
URL: https://00f.net/2026/05/17/developping-in-the-open/
Open-source governance friction threatens Bun's momentum against Node and Deno

Bun gained traction on performance claims, but this piece suggests community management issues. Runtime wars matter because they determine default toolchains for the next generation of developers. If Bun stumbles on community trust, Deno or Node improvements could recapture mindshare. Worth monitoring for anyone with portfolio exposure to JavaScript infrastructure.

### Fits on a Floppy - A Manifesto for Small Software
URL: https://fitsonafloppy.com
Counter-movement to bloatware has real implications for edge computing and embedded systems

The "small software" philosophy isn't just nostalgia—it's operationally relevant as computing moves to constrained environments: IoT, automotive, industrial sensors. Companies building for edge deployment face real binary size constraints. This manifesto articulates principles that embedded teams are already practicing out of necessity.

### I turned a $80 RK3562 Android tablet into a Debian Linux workstation
URL: https://github.com/tech4bot/rk3562deb
Sub-$100 ARM hardware running full Linux signals continued erosion of x86 assumptions

Rockchip's RK3562 enabling a usable Linux workstation at this price point is another data point in ARM's march across computing segments. Relevant for anyone modeling Intel/AMD long-term—the surface area where x86 is required keeps shrinking. Educational and emerging market deployments increasingly don't need traditional PC architecture.

## ⚡ Signal vs. Noise

The through-line today is infrastructure maturation: AI tooling is moving from "does it work" to "does it work efficiently" (Semble's token economics), hardware bets are generating liquidity events (Cerebras/Eclipse), and governance questions are becoming material risks (OpenAI trial, Bun community). The interesting tension is between the hype cycle's peak and the actual buildout phase—serious capital is now flowing to picks-and-shovels plays rather than application-layer moonshots. Watch the small-software and edge-computing threads; as AI models get larger, the systems running inference at the edge need to get leaner.
